# Privacy Policy

Version 2026-11-19 · **A first draft, not yet reviewed by a lawyer.**

What Welcome Wave holds about you, who sees it, where it goes and how to get it removed.

**For:** Everyone who signs in, and anyone who appears in a recording\
**Accepted by:** Each person, for themselves, in the product.

## In brief

- Your organisation decides what goes into Welcome Wave and is responsible for it. We run the service on its instructions.
- We hold your account details, KT recordings with their transcripts and notes, your questions and answers, your onboarding records, and the code and documents your organisation connects.
- Google's Gemini models read this content to write answers, notes and drafts. We do not train AI models on it, and we do not sell it.
- There is no advertising and there are no analytics trackers. The browser keeps your sign-in and a few preferences.
- A new hire can see everything their manager can see about them, on the page “What your manager sees”.
- An admin can export your organisation's records, erase a person's account details and conversations, or delete everything.

## 1. Who is responsible

Welcome Wave is run by the company that operates this service. In this policy that is “we” and “us”.

| Data | Who is responsible | Our part |
|---|---|---|
| What your organisation's people put into a workspace: recordings, transcripts, documents, code, questions, onboarding records | Your organisation. In legal terms it is the controller (GDPR and UK GDPR), the data fiduciary (India's DPDP Act) and the business (California's CCPA). | We handle it on your organisation's instructions, as its processor and service provider, under [Data Processing Agreement](DPA.md). |
| Your sign-in account, the record of which documents you accepted, security logs, and our dealings with customers | We are. | Controller and data fiduciary. |

For anything in a workspace, ask your organisation's admin first. We help them answer.

| Who we are | Details |
|---|---|
| Company | The company that operates this service |
| Postal address | The operator's registered office |
| Privacy requests and complaints | The privacy contact for this service |
| Other questions | The support contact for this service |

## 2. What we hold

| What | Details | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| Your account | Name, work email, role, GitHub username if you give one, and a sign-in identifier. Your password is held by Google's Identity Platform, not by us. | You; the person who invited you |
| Your organisation's setup | Teams, projects, who is on them, and invitations: email, name, role and who invited. | Admins and managers |
| KT sessions | Title, time, who booked it, attendees' email addresses and the meeting link. | Whoever books the session |
| KT recordings | The video file, with voices, faces if cameras were on, and shared screens. From it: a transcript with speaker labels, notes, action items, descriptions of what was on screen, and links to the code it explains. Also who confirmed that every participant agreed, and when. | A member who adds the file; your organisation's Google Drive |
| Questions and answers | What you ask the assistant, its answers and sources, your thumbs up or down, questions passed on to a person and their replies, and notes you leave on a document, file, session or answer. | You; the assistant |
| Onboarding records | Start date, role, team, manager and mentor; plan and tasks; milestones; access requests; documents you acknowledged; environment checks from your machine (tool names, versions, pass or fail); progress, blockers, weekly summaries, check-in answers and reviews of your pull requests. | You, your manager, GitHub, and agents' drafts a person approved |
| Surveys | Answers on a scale, with a team and a survey day, stored without your name or account id. Your onboarding record notes which survey days you have answered, so the answers are not untraceable by whoever runs the database. They are shown only as averages of five or more people. | New hires |
| Code and documents | The repositories your organisation connects, with pull requests, issues and check results, and the documents members upload. These can hold names and email addresses, for example in comments. | Your organisation's GitHub; members |
| Calendar connection | The email address of the Google account your organisation connects, and a refresh token stored encrypted. A person's Calendly link. | A manager or admin; each person |
| Records of acceptance | Which version of each document you accepted, when and how, the network your click came from (the first part of the address, never all of it) and your browser's description. | Your click |
| Audit log | Security-relevant actions: who did what, to what, and when. | The service |
| Technical logs | For each request: the path, status, timing, and your user and organisation ids. No request contents. For each AI call: the model, timing and size, never the words. | The service |

Your network (IP) address is used in memory to limit request rates. The database never holds it in full: a record of acceptance keeps the first part, and a document acknowledged before your first day keeps a keyed hash. The hosting platform's own logs record it.

If the web app crashes, it sends us the error text with email addresses, keys and tokens removed. It is written to the log and not stored anywhere else.

> We do not collect advertising identifiers or location, and the web app does not ask for your camera or microphone.

## 3. Why we use it

Workspace data is used to do what your organisation uses Welcome Wave for: answering questions with sources, writing notes of KT sessions, and planning and following an onboarding. Your organisation decides the legal ground for that. Ask it which one applies to you.

For the data we are responsible for:

| Why | What we use | Legal ground under GDPR |
|---|---|---|
| To create your account and sign you in | Name, email, sign-in identifier | Our contract with you and your organisation |
| To keep the service secure and find misuse | Audit log, technical logs, network address | Our legitimate interest in a secure service |
| To show that the documents were accepted | Records of acceptance | Our legitimate interest in being able to show agreement |
| To deal with customers: contracts, invoices, support | Admins' contact details | Our contract; legal duties such as tax records |

Under India's DPDP Act, the ground is your consent, given when you accept this policy, or a use the Act allows without consent. You can withdraw consent by leaving your organisation or asking for erasure (section 9).

The product sends no marketing. Agents draft plans, reviews and recommendations, and a person decides. Some markers update by rule: a task moves when your pull request does.

## 4. Who can see what

Nobody outside your organisation can see its data. Each organisation's records are kept apart by the database itself, not only by the application. One thing is kept apart by the application alone: the saved state of an agent run that is waiting for a person's approval.

- **Members.** Each member sees the projects they belong to: the people, code, documents, sessions and notes.
- **Recordings.** Members of the project can watch them and read the notes. Only managers and admins can open the full transcript. The assistant reads passages of it to answer members of the project, so an answer can repeat what someone said in a session.
- **Questions to the assistant.** Yours are not shown to your manager or mentor. They see a count on the code a question was about, and that the assistant answered you, when, and from which sources. Never your words.
- **Questions passed on to a person.** That person reads the question in full, with your name. When they answer, the question and the answer become a source the assistant can show to other members of the project, without your name.
- **Onboarding records.** Yours are read by you, your mentor and your project's managers. Executives see counts, never a person's words.
- **Surveys.** Answers appear only as averages, and only when five or more people answered.
- **Admins.** They read the audit log and can export all of the organisation's records, conversations included. Each export is recorded.

If you are a new hire, the page “What your manager sees” lists every item others can read about you, with who reads it and the same values they see.

People at the company that operates this service who run the servers can technically reach the database and files. They do so only when it is needed to run, secure or support the service, or when the law requires it.

## 5. AI processing

Welcome Wave uses Google's Gemini models. To build the search index, they receive the text of the code and documents your organisation connects, all of it. For a task, they receive what it needs: passages of that code and those documents, pull request changes for a review, transcripts after redaction, your question, the onboarding records an agent drafts from, and, to write a session's notes, the recording itself.

An agent chooses which of the project's records to read for a task, through a fixed set of read-only tools. No tool writes, sends or changes anything.

Before any text from a recording is stored, a redactor replaces email addresses, phone numbers, common key formats and password-like values with labels. It follows patterns: it does not remove names, voices or faces, and it can miss things.

We do not train or fine-tune AI models on your organisation's data.

Google handles what it receives under its own terms. Where the service runs on Google Cloud, the models are reached through Vertex AI, which reads a recording from the service's own file store. Where it runs on a single server, they are reached through the Gemini API with the operator's key: each recording is uploaded to Google for the analysis, and we delete that copy when the analysis finishes or fails. A copy we could not delete is removed by Google within 48 hours.

An operator on Google Cloud can set a Gemini API key as well. The Gemini API is then used in place of Vertex AI.

> **On this service.** In the product, this place says how the service you are reading it on is set up: which AI service it uses and whether tracing is on.

> **One thing to check.** On the Gemini API's free tier, Google's terms let Google use what is sent to improve its products, and let people at Google read it. On the paid tier they do not. A single-server installation that holds real data must use a paid key. If you are unsure which applies to you, ask at the privacy contact for this service.

Tracing of agent runs to LangSmith, an outside service, is off unless the operator turns it on. When it is on, LangSmith receives each traced run's prompts and outputs and keeps them for its own period. Removing a recording, erasing a person or deleting an organisation in Welcome Wave does not remove them there.

## 6. Who we share it with

- **Our providers.** The companies that host the service, sign you in and run the AI models. They are listed in [Sub-processors](SUBPROCESSORS.md).
- **Services your organisation connects.** GitHub, Google Calendar, Meet and Drive, and Calendly. A Calendly booking link carries the booker's name and email to Calendly. Google Calendar emails invitations to a session's attendees.
- **The law.** An authority, when the law requires it. We tell your organisation first where we are allowed to.
- **A successor.** A company that takes over the service in a merger or sale, under the same commitments. We tell your organisation's admins before that happens.

We do not sell personal data, and we do not share it for advertising.

## 7. Where it is kept

Where the service runs on Google Cloud, the database and files sit in one region that the operator chooses. The default is Mumbai, India. Google's job queue, its logs and its monitoring are not tied to that region. A queued job carries ids, file paths and, for a pull request, its description and its author's GitHub username. Where the service runs on a single server, the database and files sit on that server.

Sign-in is handled on Google's global infrastructure. AI requests may be served from any Google region unless the operator pins one. So your data may be processed outside your own country, including in the United States.

> **On this service.** In the product, this place says how the service you are reading it on is set up: where it runs and which AI service it uses.

Where GDPR or UK GDPR applies to such a transfer, it is made under standard contractual clauses or another mechanism those laws accept. India's DPDP Act allows transfers except to countries its government restricts.

## 8. How long we keep it

| What | How long | After that |
|---|---|---|
| Account and workspace records | For as long as your organisation uses Welcome Wave. Nothing in this row expires on its own. | Removed when an admin erases a person or deletes the organisation |
| Recording video files | On Google Cloud: 30 days, then deleted automatically. On a single server: for the number of days the operator has set, or until someone removes them when no period is set. | The notes, transcript and links to code stay until removed |
| Google's copy of a recording for analysis (single server only) | Until the analysis finishes or fails. Never more than 48 hours. | Deleted by us at Google; a copy we could not delete is deleted by Google |
| Audit log | 365 days, unless the operator sets another period. Never less than 30 days. Entries cannot be edited or removed one by one. | Deleted by the daily purge once past the period, or with the organisation |
| Invitation and pre-boarding links | They stop working after 14 days | The invitation's record stays with the organisation's records |
| Records of acceptance | Until the organisation is deleted | Deleted with it |
| Technical logs | The logging service's period: 30 days on Google Cloud unless the operator changes it | Deleted by the logging service |
| Traces at LangSmith, only when tracing is on | LangSmith's own period | Not removed by any deletion in Welcome Wave |
| Backups | On Google Cloud: a daily backup, with the last 30 kept in production and the last 7 in other environments, and 7 days of point-in-time recovery. On a single server: the backups the operator makes. | Deleted data stays in a backup until that backup expires |

> **On this service.** In the product, this place says how the service you are reading it on is set up: where it runs, how long a recording's video file is kept and how long audit entries are kept.

## 9. Your rights, and how to use them

Depending on where you live, the law gives you rights over your personal data: to see it, correct it, have it erased, take a copy, object to a use or restrict it, withdraw consent, and complain to a regulator. India's DPDP Act adds the right to name someone to act for you. California law adds the right not to be treated worse for using these rights.

For workspace data, ask your organisation. In the product:

- **See.** New hires open “What your manager sees”. Everyone sees their own questions, tasks and notifications.
- **Correct.** Change your GitHub username in Settings, Account. For your name or email, ask your admin or write to us.
- **Leave.** Settings, Account, “Leave the organisation” unbinds your sign-in from the organisation. Your records stay with it, and your sign-in account at Google stays.
- **Erase.** An admin uses Settings, Organisation, “Erase a person's data”. On your account, your name, email and GitHub username are replaced and your sign-in is unbound. You are removed from every project. Your chats, the questions you sent to a person, your notifications, scheduling link and invitations are deleted, and the reasons you wrote when asking for a recording to be removed are blanked. Your onboarding records stay under “Erased person”. Records of acceptance stay, by id.
- **Copy.** An admin uses Settings, Organisation, “Export”: the organisation's records as one file, without credentials. Stored files such as documents and videos are opened from their own pages. There is no download for one person on their own yet.
- **Remove a recording.** Ask for it on the session's page, or ask a project manager. A manager removes the video, transcript, notes and search entries in one step. Managers also delete a document from its own page.
- **Delete everything.** An admin uses Settings, Organisation, “Delete organisation”.

> **What erasing does not reach.** Erasing a person changes their account and deletes the items listed above. It does not reach copies made earlier, which can still carry your name or your words: session attendee lists; recordings and transcripts you speak in; answers a colleague verified from a question you passed on; notes you left on a document, file, session or answer; drafts waiting for approval; notices already sent to colleagues; and audit entries about an invitation, a changed GitHub username or a connected Google account, which hold that address or username until they expire. Ask your admin to remove a recording or a document that names you. Backups keep deleted data until they expire.

Erasing a person, leaving an organisation and deleting an organisation do not remove the sign-in account at Google's Identity Platform, because one sign-in can belong to other organisations. Write to the privacy contact for this service and we remove it.

For data we are responsible for, or if your organisation does not answer, write to the privacy contact for this service. We reply within the time the law sets.

## 10. What your browser stores

No advertising or analytics cookies. The web app uses one short-lived cookie and the browser's own storage.

| Stored | Where | What for | How long |
|---|---|---|---|
| ww\_google\_state | A cookie, sent only to one address of this service | Ties Google's consent page to your browser when a manager connects Google Calendar | 10 minutes |
| Your sign-in | The browser's database (IndexedDB), kept by Google's sign-in library | Keeps you signed in | Until you sign out |
| Preferences: ww-theme, ww-signed-in, ww-project, ww-board, ww-tour, ww-palette-recent, ww-audit-rows | Local storage | Light or dark, the project and person you last opened, code-tour progress, recent commands, rows per page | Until you clear them |
| This tab: ww-scroll, ww-routes, ww-chunk-reload, ww-boot-words | Session storage | Scroll positions, how answers in the open chat were routed, one reload after an update, the intro's words | Until you close the tab |

If you choose to sign in with Google, Google's own window sets Google's cookies on Google's domains. If the operator has turned on sign-in protection, Google's reCAPTCHA loads on the sign-in page.

## 11. Security

Sign-in is verified on every request, and roles decide what each person can do. Each organisation's records are kept apart in the database. Connections use HTTPS. Admins can read an audit log of security-relevant actions.

The full list of measures, and what is not in place yet, is in Annex 2 of [Data Processing Agreement](DPA.md).

## 12. Children

Welcome Wave is for people at work and is not meant for anyone under 18. Do not add a child's personal data. If we learn that we hold some, we remove it.

## 13. Changes to this policy

Each version carries its date. When a new version is published, you are asked to accept it in the product.

## 14. Questions and complaints

Write to the privacy contact for this service. This is also the address for a grievance under India's DPDP Act.

You may also complain to the data protection authority where you live or work.
